epic.title: Cloud Abstraction Layer
epic.description: Build the cloud abstraction layer (spec §9): the four cloud-agnostic traits (ObjectStore, ObjectLock, ReplicatedKv, Hsm) in cloud-types, plus the cloud-memory, cloud-aws, cloud-localstack, and cloud-softhsm backend crates, wired through a Backend factory selected by runtime config and Cargo features. A shared cloud-test-suite crate guarantees behavioral consistency by running identical conformance suites against every backend — memory in unit tests, AWS via LocalStack, and SoftHSM2 via PKCS#11 — all runnable on a laptop with zero cloud spend (§1, §18).

tickets.title: Define cloud-types crate: ObjectStore, ObjectLock, ReplicatedKv, Hsm traits
tickets.description:
## Goal
Create `crates/cloud-types` with the four async cloud-capability traits, common DTOs, and error taxonomy per spec §9.1/§9.3, including `is_fips_validated()` on `Hsm` per §14.4. This is the critical-path anchor that blocks all storage and CA service work (§25.5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Crate `cloud-types` exists with modules `object_store.rs`, `object_lock.rs`, `replicated_kv.rs`, `hsm.rs`, `errors.rs` (§9.3)
- `ObjectStore`: `put/get/head/list/delete`; `PutOptions` supports if-not-exists (no-overwrite) semantics upholding the append-only invariant (§8, §9.7 `test_overwrite_fails`)
- `ObjectLock`: `put_with_retention`, `extend_retention`, `get_retention` (§9.1)
- `ReplicatedKv`: `get`, conditional `put`, `atomic_update`, `transact`, `query` plus `Key`/`Item`/`Value`/`Condition`/`UpdateExpression`/`Operation` DTOs (§9.1)
- `Hsm`: `sign`, `get_public_key`, `generate_key`, and `is_fips_validated() -> bool` (§14.4)
- Error taxonomy distinguishes `NotFound`, `ConditionFailed`, `AlreadyExists`, `RetentionViolation`, and retryable transport errors
- All traits object-safe and usable as `Arc<dyn Trait>` with `Send + Sync` bounds (§9.4)
- Rustdoc on every method states the required capability bar from §9.5

## Out of Scope
- Any backend implementation (memory/AWS/SoftHSM tickets); `Backend` factory (cloud-backend-factory); storage facade and tile cache (storage-facade epic)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): compile-time object-safety assertions (`Arc<dyn Trait>` usage), error-classification helper tests; no external dependencies

## Demo
`cargo doc -p cloud-types --open` shows the four documented traits; `cargo test -p cloud-types` green.

tickets.title: cloud-memory: pure in-memory implementation of all four cloud traits
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement `crates/cloud-memory` — pure-memory implementations of all four `cloud-types` traits so every downstream crate can unit test with zero external dependencies (§9.3, §9.6). Second cloud-abstraction priority on the critical path (§25.5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `MemoryObjectStore`: map-backed put/get/head/list/delete; rejects overwrite with `AlreadyExists` when `PutOptions` requires if-not-exists (§9.7)
- `MemoryObjectLock`: retention windows enforced against an injectable `Clock` (§22.11, §18.4 pattern); `extend_retention` forward-only; delete during retention rejected with `RetentionViolation` (§9.5)
- `MemoryReplicatedKv`: conditional put, `atomic_update`, all-or-nothing `transact`, prefix `query`; shareable as `Arc<dyn ReplicatedKv>` across tokio tasks with interior locking, no `unsafe`
- Property test: 100 concurrent tokio tasks racing conditional puts on one key yield exactly one `Ok` per round; `transact` with one failing condition applies zero ops (§19.2)
- `MemoryHsm`: ECDSA P-256 via RustCrypto `p256` (§14.1); `generate_key`/`sign`/`get_public_key`; `is_fips_validated() == false` (§14.4)
- Zero external dependencies: no Docker, no LocalStack, no SoftHSM (§9.6)
- Full crate test run completes fast enough for the <30s unit budget (§19.1)

## Out of Scope
- Shared conformance suite definitions (cloud-test-suite tickets); `Backend` factory wiring; persistence of any kind

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1) per trait impl
- Property (`proptest`, §19.2): concurrent conditional CAS admits exactly one winner; `transact` never partially applies

## Demo
With Docker stopped: `cargo test -p cloud-memory` — all green, sub-second.

tickets.title: cloud-test-suite: shared ObjectStore + ObjectLock conformance suites
tickets.description:
## Goal
Create `crates/cloud-test-suite` with the factory-closure suite pattern from §9.7 and ship the `ObjectStore` and `ObjectLock` suites, validated against `cloud-memory`. Every backend (current and future GCP/Azure) must pass these identical tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Crate `cloud-test-suite` with generic `run_object_store_suite(factory)` matching the §9.7 signature shape
- ObjectStore suite covers: put/get round-trip, overwrite-fails under if-not-exists, list-with-prefix, head metadata, delete, get-missing returns `NotFound`
- `run_object_lock_suite` covers: `put_with_retention` + `get_retention` round-trip, extend forward-only (shortening rejected), delete during retention rejected (§9.5 append-only bar)
- Both suites wired in `cloud-memory/tests/` and passing (§9.7)
- Suite helpers usable from other crates' `tests/` dirs without copy-paste

## Out of Scope
- ReplicatedKv and Hsm suites (cloud-test-suite-kv, cloud-test-suite-hsm); running suites against AWS/SoftHSM backends (conformance tickets)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): suites executed against the memory backend prove the suite itself; suites become the integration layer when backend crates adopt them

## Demo
`cargo test -p cloud-memory` output shows `object_store_suite` and `object_lock_suite` cases passing.

tickets.title: cloud-test-suite: shared ReplicatedKv conformance suite
tickets.description:
## Goal
Add `run_replicated_kv_suite` to `cloud-test-suite` (§9.7) covering the conditional-write and transactional semantics the lease/epoch protocol and write path depend on (§8.3, §9.5), validated against `cloud-memory`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Suite covers: get/put round-trip; conditional put success and `ConditionFailed` on violated condition; `atomic_update` with condition expression; `transact` is all-or-nothing when one op's condition fails; `query` returns all items under a prefix
- Property test (`proptest`, §19.2): N concurrent conditional CAS attempts on the same key yield exactly one success per round — the invariant multi-region leasing builds on (§9.5 "Conditional KV writes")
- Suite wired in `cloud-memory/tests/` and passing
- Failure-mode assertions use the shared `cloud-types` error taxonomy, not backend-specific errors

## Out of Scope
- Running against DynamoDB/LocalStack (cloud-aws-conformance); lease/epoch protocol itself (multi-region epic); Kani harnesses for index allocation (storage-facade epic)

## Testing
- Unit + property (§19.1, §19.2) against memory backend; reused as integration suite by backend crates

## Demo
`cargo test -p cloud-memory` shows `replicated_kv_suite` cases including the concurrent-CAS property test passing.

tickets.title: cloud-test-suite: shared Hsm conformance suite
tickets.description:
## Goal
Add `run_hsm_suite` to `cloud-test-suite` (§9.7) so every HSM backend (memory, SoftHSM, later CloudHSM) proves identical signing behavior, validated against `MemoryHsm`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Suite covers: `generate_key(EcdsaP256)` → `get_public_key` → `sign` → signature verifies with a RustCrypto `p256` verifier (§14.1, §19.6 cryptographic invariant style)
- Signing with an unknown `KeyHandle` returns a typed error, never a panic
- Suite signature takes `expected_fips: bool` and asserts `is_fips_validated() == expected_fips` (§14.4); memory run passes `false`
- Deterministic message set plus a small randomized message property case
- Suite wired in `cloud-memory/tests/` and passing

## Out of Scope
- SoftHSM/PKCS#11 execution of this suite (cloud-softhsm-conformance); key rotation and cross-region key replication ceremonies (multi-region epic, §14.2); ML-DSA (v2, core-mtc-library feature flag)

## Testing
- Unit + light property (§19.1, §19.2) against memory backend; becomes the integration suite for cloud-softhsm

## Demo
`cargo test -p cloud-memory` shows `hsm_suite` sign/verify round-trip passing.

tickets.title: cloud-aws crate: S3ObjectStore and S3ObjectLock implementations
tickets.description:
## Goal
Create `crates/cloud-aws` and implement `ObjectStore` and `ObjectLock` over `aws-sdk-s3` (§9.3), exercised exclusively against LocalStack — no real AWS spend (§1 non-goals).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Crate scaffolding with `s3_object_store.rs` and `s3_object_lock.rs` per the §9.3 layout
- `S3ObjectStore`: put (If-None-Match for no-overwrite semantics), get, head, paginated list, delete
- `S3ObjectLock`: retention via S3 Object Lock; COMPLIANCE-mode semantics and any LocalStack emulation caveats documented in rustdoc (§9.5 retention bar)
- SDK errors mapped onto the `cloud-types` error taxonomy (retryable vs terminal, `ConditionFailed`/`AlreadyExists` on precondition failure)
- Client construction accepts injected endpoint/credentials config so LocalStack and (hypothetically) real AWS use the same code path
- Integration tests gated behind `--features integration` (§19.1) and green against LocalStack

## Out of Scope
- DynamoDB `ReplicatedKv` (cloud-aws-ddb-kv); CloudHSM (cloud-aws-cloudhsm); running the shared suites in CI (cloud-aws-conformance); S3 bucket layout/schema (storage-facade epic)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): error-mapping and request-shaping tests without network
- Integration (§19.1): LocalStack-backed tests behind `--features integration`

## Demo
`docker compose up -d localstack && cargo test -p cloud-aws --features integration` green.

tickets.title: cloud-aws: DynamoDB ReplicatedKv implementation
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement `ReplicatedKv` over `aws-sdk-dynamodb` in `cloud-aws/src/ddb_replicated_kv.rs` (§9.3), providing the conditional and transactional writes the lease/epoch protocol and write-path linearization require (§9.5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `Condition` DTOs translated to DynamoDB `ConditionExpression`s; `ConditionalCheckFailedException` maps to `ConditionFailed` (never a panic or opaque error)
- `atomic_update` → `UpdateItem` with `UpdateExpression`; returns the updated `Item`
- `transact` → `TransactWriteItems`, all-or-nothing including per-op conditions
- `query` → prefix query against the table key schema; pagination handled
- Item/Value serialization to and from DynamoDB `AttributeValue` covered by round-trip tests
- Integration tests gated `--features integration`, green against LocalStack DynamoDB (§19.1)

## Out of Scope
- Global Tables replication semantics and multi-region simulation (multi-region epic); DDB table schema for batches/leases (storage-facade epic, §8.2); shared-suite CI wiring (cloud-aws-conformance)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): expression translation + AttributeValue round-trips
- Integration (§19.1): conditional write, atomic update, transact tests vs LocalStack

## Demo
`docker compose up -d localstack && cargo test -p cloud-aws --features integration` shows DDB KV tests passing.

tickets.title: cloud-localstack helper crate: endpoint-configured AWS backends for dev/test
tickets.description:
## Goal
Create `crates/cloud-localstack` — thin wrappers that configure the `cloud-aws` implementations with LocalStack endpoints, credentials, and path-style addressing (§9.3), so dev and test code never hand-rolls SDK endpoint config.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `cloud_localstack::build(cfg)` returns `cloud-aws` ObjectStore/ObjectLock/ReplicatedKv instances pointed at LocalStack (§9.4 `Provider::Localstack` target)
- Endpoint resolution: explicit config first, then `LOCALSTACK_ENDPOINT`-style env fallback with sane compose defaults (§18.1)
- Dummy-credential and path-style-addressing quirks handled here, not by callers
- Helper used by `cloud-aws` integration tests to construct clients (replacing ad-hoc config)
- Rustdoc quickstart: two-line example constructing a LocalStack-backed store

## Out of Scope
- The docker-compose LocalStack environment itself (foundation-infra localstack-dev-env); Backend factory wiring (cloud-backend-factory-aws); multi-region multi-instance LocalStack simulation (multi-region epic, §18.3)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): config/endpoint resolution logic
- Integration (§19.1): smoke test constructing each client and performing one round-trip vs LocalStack, gated `--features integration`

## Demo
`docker compose up -d localstack && cargo test -p cloud-localstack --features integration` green.

tickets.title: Run shared conformance suites against cloud-aws via LocalStack in CI
tickets.description:
## Goal
Wire the shared `cloud-test-suite` suites (ObjectStore, ObjectLock, ReplicatedKv) against the `cloud-aws` backend through `cloud-localstack`, per the §9.7 pattern, and run them in a CI integration lane — guaranteeing behavioral consistency between memory and AWS backends.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `cloud-aws/tests/` invokes `run_object_store_suite`, `run_object_lock_suite`, and `run_replicated_kv_suite` with factories built via `cloud-localstack` (§9.7)
- All suites green against LocalStack, gated `--features integration` (§19.1)
- CI gains an integration job with a LocalStack service container running these suites on every PR touching cloud crates
- Any genuine behavioral divergence (e.g., LocalStack Object Lock gaps) is either fixed in the backend or skipped via `#[ignore = "reason"]` carrying a tracking-ticket reference — shared suites are never edited to accommodate one backend

## Out of Scope
- Hsm suite vs SoftHSM (cloud-softhsm-conformance); chaos/failure-injection scenarios (testing-infrastructure epic, §19.9); performance benchmarks (§19.11)

## Testing
- Integration (§19.1): this ticket IS the integration coverage; reuses unit-proven suites

## Demo
CI run shows the `cloud-integration` job green; locally `docker compose up -d localstack && cargo test -p cloud-aws --features integration` runs the identical suites.

tickets.title: cloud-softhsm: PKCS#11 Hsm implementation against SoftHSM2
tickets.description:
## Goal
Create `crates/cloud-softhsm` implementing the `Hsm` trait over PKCS#11 (via `cryptoki`) against SoftHSM2 — the dev-mode stand-in for CloudHSM (§9.3, §14, §18.1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `generate_key` creates an ECDSA P-256 keypair (v1 algorithm, §14.1) and returns a stable `KeyHandle` (token label/ID based)
- `get_public_key` exports SPKI DER; `sign` produces a signature that verifies with a RustCrypto `p256` verifier; signature encoding choice documented for checkpoint-signer consumers
- Slot/token/PIN configuration via config struct with env fallback; token bootstrap script (init token + PIN) usable by both tests and `make demo` (§18.1)
- `is_fips_validated() == false` — dev-only, explicitly non-FIPS (§14.4)
- Concurrent signing: integration test spawns 8 tokio tasks signing in parallel; all signatures verify and no PKCS#11 `CKR_*` errors occur (sessions pooled or per-operation, never shared across threads)
- Integration tests gated `--features integration`, green with SoftHSM2 installed

## Out of Scope
- CloudHSM wiring (cloud-aws-cloudhsm); cross-region key replication ceremony (multi-region epic, §14.2); checkpoint signer component (ca-service epic); ML-DSA keys (v2)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): config parsing, handle encoding, error mapping (mock-free logic only)
- Integration (§19.1): sign/verify round-trip vs SoftHSM2; latency smoke assertion far under the 100ms p99 target (§14.3)

## Demo
`./scripts/softhsm-init.sh && cargo test -p cloud-softhsm --features integration` green.

tickets.title: Run shared Hsm suite against SoftHSM2 in CI
tickets.description:
## Goal
Wire `run_hsm_suite` from `cloud-test-suite` against `cloud-softhsm` (§9.7) and run it in the CI integration lane, proving the PKCS#11 backend behaves identically to `MemoryHsm`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `cloud-softhsm/tests/` invokes `run_hsm_suite` with a factory that provisions a fresh SoftHSM2 token per run (§9.7 pattern), gated `--features integration` (§19.1)
- CI integration job installs/initializes SoftHSM2 (reusing the softhsm-backend bootstrap script) and runs the suite on every PR touching HSM crates
- Suite invoked with `expected_fips == false` for SoftHSM (§14.4)
- Token setup/teardown leaves no state between test runs (idempotent re-runs)

## Out of Scope
- New suite cases (extend cloud-test-suite-hsm instead); CloudHSM validation (cloud-aws-cloudhsm, untestable without spend per §1); checkpoint-signer E2E (ca-service epic)

## Testing
- Integration (§19.1): this ticket is the SoftHSM integration coverage, reusing the unit-proven shared suite

## Demo
CI shows the HSM integration job green; locally `./scripts/softhsm-init.sh && cargo test -p cloud-softhsm --features integration` runs the shared suite.

tickets.title: Backend struct and build_backend factory with Memory provider
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement the §9.4 `Backend` factory: the struct of four `Arc<dyn Trait>` handles plus `build_backend(BackendConfig)` with a `Provider` enum, shipping `Provider::Memory` first so downstream CA-service work can start immediately against a fully wired backend.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `Backend { object_store, object_lock, replicated_kv, hsm }` as `Arc<dyn ...>` fields exactly per §9.4
- `Provider` enum with `Memory`, `Aws`, `Localstack` variants (§9.4); non-memory variants return a clear `Unimplemented` error until cloud-backend-factory-aws lands
- `build_backend` returns a working all-memory `Backend`; consumers depend only on `cloud-types` + factory, never name a concrete backend (§9.3, §9.4)
- Cargo features gate backend crate dependencies so memory-only consumers do not compile the AWS SDK (§9.3 "wired via Cargo features")
- `BackendConfig` deserializes from config file/env (serde); unknown provider strings rejected with actionable error
- Doc example shows a service constructor taking `Arc<Backend>` (§9.4 `CaService::new` shape)

## Out of Scope
- Aws/Localstack/SoftHSM wiring (cloud-backend-factory-aws); GCP/Azure/on-prem variants (multi-cloud epic, §27); storage facade construction (storage-facade epic)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): config deserialization, memory build round-trip (put/get through `Backend`), feature-flag compile checks in CI matrix

## Demo
`cargo test -p cloud-backend` green with no Docker; doc example compiles via doctest.

tickets.title: Wire Aws and Localstack providers into build_backend
tickets.description:
## Goal
Complete the §9.4 factory: `Provider::Aws` → `cloud_aws::build`, `Provider::Localstack` → `cloud_localstack::build`, with SoftHSM wired as the HSM for dev/Localstack profiles so a full four-trait `Backend` is buildable outside memory mode.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `build_backend` with `Provider::Localstack` returns a `Backend` backed by LocalStack S3/DDB via `cloud-localstack` and SoftHSM for `hsm` (§14: SoftHSM in dev)
- `Provider::Aws` path implemented and feature-gated; HSM slot documented as CloudHSM-pending (no real AWS spend, §1) with config validation only
- Backend crates remain feature-gated: memory-only builds compile without AWS SDK or PKCS#11 deps (§9.3)
- `BackendConfig` gains `aws`/`localstack` sections matching §9.4's `cfg.aws`/`cfg.localstack`
- Integration smoke test: `build_backend(localstack cfg)` then one put/get and one HSM sign through the `Backend` handles

## Out of Scope
- CloudHSM implementation (cloud-aws-cloudhsm); GCP/Azure/on-prem providers (multi-cloud epic); dev-env compose orchestration (foundation-infra)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): provider dispatch + config validation
- Integration (§19.1): LocalStack+SoftHSM smoke test gated `--features integration`

## Demo
`docker compose up -d localstack && ./scripts/softhsm-init.sh && cargo test -p cloud-backend --features integration` builds a live `Backend` and round-trips all four capabilities.

tickets.title: cloud-aws: CloudHSM Hsm implementation via PKCS#11 (config-validated, no cloud spend)
tickets.description:
## Goal
Add `cloudhsm.rs` to `cloud-aws` (§9.3): an `Hsm` implementation reusing the PKCS#11 core from `cloud-softhsm`, configured for the CloudHSM client library — keeping the v1 production design honest (§14) without violating the no-AWS-spend constraint (§1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `CloudHsm` implements `Hsm` by delegating to the shared PKCS#11 session layer with CloudHSM-specific module path, cluster cert, and CU credential config (§14.2 Option A context documented)
- `is_fips_validated() == true` for this backend, per §14.4 (FIPS comes from the HSM itself); rustdoc states validation is inherited from hardware, not the binary
- Config validation unit-tested: missing cluster cert / bad module path produce typed errors
- Crate compiles and passes `cargo clippy` with the feature enabled; explicitly marked untested-against-real-hardware in rustdoc and README (§1 non-goals: no production deployment)
- SoftHSM-backed test exercises the shared PKCS#11 code path this impl delegates to

## Out of Scope
- Real CloudHSM cluster provisioning or CDK for HSM (no spend, §1); cross-region key replication ceremony (multi-region epic, §14.2); FIPS CI release gates (§14.4, foundation-infra/ca-service hardening)

## Testing
- Unit (§19.1): config validation, module resolution; shared-path coverage via SoftHSM integration tests

## Demo
`cargo build -p cloud-aws --features cloudhsm && cargo test -p cloud-aws cloudhsm` shows config-validation tests green.

tickets.title: Document capability bar and how-to-add-a-backend guide
tickets.description:
## Goal
Write the cloud-abstraction documentation the spec assigns this layer: the capability requirements table (§9.5), what is deliberately NOT abstracted and why (§9.2), and a step-by-step guide for adding a new backend validated by the shared suites (§9.7) — the on-ramp for post-v1 GCP/Azure/on-prem work (§27 pointer only).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `docs/cloud-backends.md` (linked from README/AGENTS.md) containing: the §9.5 capability table with required behaviors and rationale; the §9.2 abstraction boundary principle ("abstract inside the service binary, not the deployment topology"); honest cost accounting summary (§9.8)
- "Adding a backend" walkthrough: implement the four traits, pass every `cloud-test-suite` suite, wire the `Backend` factory + Cargo feature — with `cloud-memory` as the worked example
- Crate-level rustdoc for `cloud-types` links to this doc; `cargo doc` renders without warnings
- Statement that a backend lacking any §9.5 capability "isn't a fit" — abstractions do not paper over missing capabilities

## Out of Scope
- Actual GCP/Azure/on-prem implementations (multi-cloud epic); storage facade docs (storage-facade epic); runbooks (§21, observability/ops epics)

## Testing
- Doc build check (`cargo doc` warning-free) and link check in CI docs lane; doctest for any embedded code snippets (§19.1 unit)

## Demo
Open `docs/cloud-backends.md` in the repo; `cargo doc -p cloud-types --open` shows the linked guide.
